clue.text: Do up tavern, one gutted for redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds something into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
a gutted thing has lost its insides, so only the outside letters of the word one remain

explanation.surface: A tired pub is to be refurbished, with one part stripped out for the new scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves OE from 'one'; 'for redevelopment' rearranges TAVERN plus OE.
explanation.definitionFit: To do up a building is to refurbish it, restoring it to good condition.

clue.text: Man about to join ship for return journey

parts.note: Reg is a man's name
re means about or concerning
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor and a vessel prepare for the voyage home.
explanation.definitionFit: Regress as a noun means a going back, a return to an earlier place or state.

clue.text: Fool, one losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: An idiot is someone who has lost their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the U from UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nit is British slang for a silly person, short for nitwit.

clue.text: Very typical article put out, full of spite

indicators.note: putting the article out removes it from the word

parts.note: indicative means typical or characteristic of something
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A highly characteristic item is thrown out with malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes the article A, a stock crossword device; 'Very' is the usual abbreviation V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindictive describes someone seeking revenge, spiteful and wanting to hurt.

clue.text: Woman's house with sculptures erected outside?

indicators.note: the reversed word goes outside, around the house letters
erected means set upright, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: sculptures are works of art

explanation.surface: A lady's home has statues put up around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' reverses only in a down clue, where the letters read upwards; 'outside' wraps the turned word around the house abbreviation. The question mark flags the playful image.
explanation.definitionFit: Thora is a woman's first name, as in the actress Thora Hird.

clue.text: Tool fractures under pressure

definitions.meaning: a cutting tool with two blades, like big scissors
in physics, a material that breaks under sideways stress is said to do this

explanation.surface: A tool cracks when too much force is put on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden clippers are a tool, and a metal bolt that snaps under sideways stress does the same thing.

clue.text: Person who is aggressive in hospital and clumsy, putting ward off

parts.note: H is the sign for hospital

indicators.note: putting the word off means removing it

parts.note: awkward means clumsy
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aggressive patient is clumsy and shoves a ward aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a violent patient; 'putting ... off' drops the word ward from its longer synonym, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a hawk favours force and confrontation, the opposite of a dove.

clue.text: Change involves Conservative in row

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an alteration is a change

explanation.surface: A political change sparks a quarrel with a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' puts C inside ALTERATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel, which is what a row means.

clue.text: Regretful about church practice being aligned with the devil?

definitions.text: practice being aligned with the devil?

indicators.note: the sorry word goes about, around the church letters

parts.note: sorry means regretful
CE is Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone repentant about the church dabbles in devil worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the regret word around the Church of England abbreviation; the question mark admits the definition is descriptive rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is black magic, a practice traditionally thought to draw on demonic powers.

clue.text: Contract worker joining nasty women's company

indicators.note: the worker joins on to the end of the company word

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
a worker ant

explanation.surface: An employee signs up with a gang of unpleasant women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty women' is witches; their company is a COVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding agreement, a kind of contract.

clue.text: Bath visitor may well land up in trouble

definitions.meaning: Bath is an English spa city famous for its hot springs, so a visitor there might well bathe in heated springwater
to end up in a difficult or awkward predicament

explanation.surface: A tourist to the spa city ends up in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Somerset city built around Roman hot springs; the capital B hides that it is a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for ending up in a difficult situation or facing someone's anger.

clue.text: Kills time? Orders one bit of time to be killed!

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: killing a letter removes it from the word

parts.note: dictates means gives orders
T is the standard abbreviation for time, one of the two in the word dictates

explanation.surface: Someone wastes time, and a command goes out to cut a moment out of the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kills time' looks like the phrase to solve, but the definition is just 'Kills'; 'to be killed' removes only one of the two T's, since the clue says 'one bit of time'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out entirely, a near synonym of killing off.

clue.text: An attractive part of a mountainous journey in a difficult situation

definitions.text: An attractive part of a mountainous journey
definitions.meaning: a pleasing route through the mountains, read literally
a sorry state of affairs, a mess

explanation.surface: A scenic mountain route leaves the traveller in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an awkward or regrettable state of affairs.

clue.text: Emergence of Excalibur initially from mysterious lake

indicators.note: the letter emerging from the word comes out of it, so it is removed

parts.note: eerie means strange and mysterious

indicators.note: initially signals the first letter of Excalibur

explanation.surface: King Arthur's sword rises out of an uncanny lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emergence of' ... 'from' takes the E of Excalibur out of EERIE. The surface recalls the Lady of the Lake raising Arthur's sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Having heavenly body, a certain woman capturing hearts — one that's seductive

indicators.note: the outer letters capture the inner ones, holding them inside

parts.note: a comet is a body in the heavens
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts
I is the Roman numeral one
her refers to a particular woman

explanation.surface: A shapely woman steals hearts and becomes a temptress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having heavenly body' looks like praise of a woman's figure; 'capturing' sets the hearts card abbreviation and Roman one inside the joined comet-and-woman string.
explanation.definitionFit: A come-hither look is an inviting, alluring one, which is to say seductive.

clue.text: Withdraw from match on account of injury

definitions.meaning: to pull a competitor or horse out of an event before it starts
a minor cut or graze on the skin

explanation.surface: A player pulls out of a game because they are hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or athlete pulled out of a race is said to be removed, and a small skin wound is another sense.

clue.text: Worry about group in promiscuous activity

indicators.note: the worry word goes about, around the group

parts.note: to harry is to harass or worry
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Concern over a gang involved in sleeping around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the worry verb around the group word; harry here means pester, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlotry is the behaviour of a harlot, an old word for prostitution or wantonness.

clue.text: Order a learner to stop any eccentricity

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so these letters are put inside the word any

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
L is the learner sign on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Someone commands a pupil to halt any oddity in behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' means plug, so the three small pieces go inside the clue's own word any. OM (Order of Merit) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something irregular or peculiar, much as an eccentricity is a departure from the norm.

clue.text: Recover from urge to versify

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: Someone tries to shake off a sudden impulse to write poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like part of the phrasal verb in the definition, but the definition is just 'Recover'; 'from' points into 'urge to versify', whose letters run on unbroken.
explanation.definitionFit: To get over an illness or setback is to recover from it.

clue.text: Girl will get cheated going after a noble man

indicators.note: the cheated word comes after the a

parts.note: gal is a girl
had means cheated, as in I've been had

explanation.surface: A woman is deceived by a supposedly honourable man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going after' sets HAD after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the purest Knight of the Round Table, stands for a chivalrous, noble man.

clue.text: Those places offering a quick tyre change can be hell!

definitions.text: Those places offering a quick tyre change
definitions.meaning: in motor racing, cars stop in the pit lane bays for fresh tyres
something dreadful, the worst of all

explanation.surface: Motor racing's service bays can feel like torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the worst possible thing is called this, as bad as hell itself.

clue.text: Poet's cry: what's up?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a yell is a cry
eh is a questioning what, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A poet shouts out, asking what is the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole string, cry plus what's, in this down clue; reading 'what's' as EH plus S is a quirky but fair liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Lots of drama with no quiet songs

indicators.note: having no quiet means the P is dropped

parts.note: plays are many pieces of drama
P is piano, the musical term for quietly

explanation.surface: A theatre programme packed with drama but no soft songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops the P (piano, quiet in music) from PLAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is an old word for a ballad or song, so lays are songs.

clue.text: Comic panel misbehaving, doing what's expected

indicators.note: letters that misbehave are out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A panel of comedians acts up instead of behaving as they should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges the ten letters of COMIC PANEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliance means conforming to rules or demands, behaving as required.

clue.text: Tool in flat

definitions.meaning: a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood
a level surface, as in geometry

explanation.surface: A tool lying in an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woodworking implement, and in geometry the word means a level two-dimensional surface.

clue.text: Sensation when Scottish university suffers 50% cut

indicators.note: losing half the letters leaves only the first half

parts.note: Stirling is a university town in Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish university causes a fuss by halving its budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers 50% cut' keeps the first half of STIRLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or excitement, a sensation that grabs attention.

clue.text: The bloke involved with a rather big hit record

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A man gets mixed up with a fairly successful song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges THE BLOKE and A RATHER together. The answer is Elvis Presley's 1956 hit single.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's first number-one record in America was this 1956 song.

clue.text: Pull away from the East?

explanation.surface: Drag something away from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a vehicle with a rope is to haul it, and read as two words it means heading west.

clue.text: See small son taking external knock

indicators.note: the outer word takes the letter in, staying external to it

parts.note: to knock something is to criticise it, which is what decry means
S is the abbreviation, the shortened form, of son

explanation.surface: A little boy gets criticised from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking external' puts S inside DECRY: the knock word wraps around the son.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is to catch sight of something, a literary word for seeing.

clue.text: Sign of sorrow far from home? It's tough

parts.note: a tear is shed in sadness
a team playing away is not at home

explanation.surface: Weeping because one is far from home is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tough' is the noun, a rough young troublemaker, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless young hooligan is a rough type, so the word suits a tough as a noun.
